transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, hi there. It's nice to meet you too. I guess I'm here because... well, my daughter suggested it. I just feel like I’m always up and moving, you know? Like, even on a quiet Tuesday, I’m bouncing from updating the garden club phone tree to digging through my knitting bag to sorting out travel papers for that cruise we're taking next spring... before I’ve really finished any one of those things. Speaking of the cruise, we're going to Alaska! I've always wanted to see the glaciers before they melt. My husband, bless his heart, he wanted to go to the Caribbean again, but I told him, "Frank, we've done the beach, let's see some ice!" He gets sunburned so easily anyway, you'd think he'd prefer the cold. But yes, I just... I can't seem to just sit still and finish a task.
During these times when you're especially active and jumping between things, do you also feel unusually euphoric or 'on top of the world'?

Euphoric? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I'm just... busy. I don't feel like I'm on top of the world or anything strange like that. I mean, I have my good days, of course! Like when my granddaughter comes over. She just turned seven, and oh, she is just a delight. We went to the park on Sunday and she found one of those little painted rocks hidden in the bushes by the swings. Have you seen those around? People paint them with little ladybugs or sunflowers and just leave them around town for folks to find. I think it's such a sweet community thing. 

I actually went to the craft store on Monday to buy some paints to make my own, but they have so many different kinds of acrylics now, I couldn't decide. I ended up talking to the cashier for twenty minutes about her sister's cat who got stuck in a storm drain.
Thinking back to when you were a child, were you already the kind of person who had trouble staying focused on one task?
Oh my, yes. It’s funny you ask that, because even way back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was a bright girl, but just completely scattered.
When you have trouble finishing a task, is it usually because your mind is busy with worries?

Worries? Oh, goodness no. I wouldn't say I'm a worrier at all. Now, Frank, my husband, he is the worrier in the family. Bless him, he watches that 24-hour news channel all day and gets so worked up about the weather reports. Just yesterday he was pacing around fretting about a storm coming in, and I told him, "Frank, we have a perfectly good roof!" 

Which actually reminded me, we really do need to get the gutters cleaned before all the oak leaves fall.
